title: Measurement and data health
purpose: When I am about to move money on a number, open Measurement to check that the number is right, fresh and counted once, so I do not act on a broken tag, a double claim or a stale report.
fires: the agency's platform screenshots, the analyst's monthly tracking audit, the Slack thread asking which number is right, and the habit of trusting whichever dashboard looks best.
not_for: a store with one channel and small ad spend, where store orders and the bank balance are all the truth it needs.

jobs.job: When a site change quietly stops the purchase tag from firing, tell me the same day, so I do not spend 3 weeks cutting ads that were working
jobs.circumstance: a theme update or new checkout app went live on Thursday, Meta shows sales falling, the store's orders are steady, nobody has connected the two

progress.functional: know the day tracking broke, which events stopped and on which platforms
progress.emotional: stop the dread that every number might be quietly wrong
progress.social: avoid the call where I explain to a partner we cut good ads for weeks

jobs.hire_today: a developer or agency who checks when someone complains, a tracking app, or nothing
jobs.fire: the monthly tracking audit and the habit of finding breaks only when a platform number looks strange

forces.push: every day it runs broken, ad platforms learn from the wrong data and budget decisions go wrong
forces.pull: a same-day flag when tracked purchases split from store orders, with the likely cause
forces.habit: the agency says the tracking is fine
forces.anxiety: what if it cries wolf on normal daily swings

jobs.little_hire: every morning, and after every site, app or consent change

watch.metric: tracked purchases per platform divided by store orders, daily
watch.source: Shopify orders, Meta events, GA4 purchases

drives.metric: days per quarter with a purchase tracking gap over 10 percent

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: purchase tag broken for 21 days, 2 good campaigns paused. After: breaks found within 24 hours, 0 campaigns cut on broken data.
jobs.not_for: a store with no paid ads and no one reading platform numbers

jobs.job: When I open the Monday report and something looks off, tell me if a number is a day stale or missing a feed before I act, so I do not cut budget on a half day of data
jobs.circumstance: Monday 8 am, the weekly numbers look down 15 percent, a sync failed overnight, the media buyer is waiting for a call

progress.functional: know which numbers are fresh, which are late and which feeds failed
progress.emotional: stop acting on numbers I half trust
progress.social: give the buyer a call I will not have to take back

jobs.hire_today: an analyst who checks the pipes, the agency, or nothing because freshness is invisible
jobs.fire: the habit of assuming the report is current because it loaded

forces.push: a stale number leads to a wrong cut or a wrong scale
forces.pull: each number shown with its age and a pass or fail before I read it
forces.habit: reports have always just been there
forces.anxiety: what if the check itself is wrong

jobs.little_hire: every morning before the first decision

watch.metric: share of headline numbers that passed the freshness check this morning, daily
watch.source: sync logs for store, ad platforms, GA4 and email

drives.metric: decisions reversed because the data was stale, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 budget cuts last quarter made on a report missing a day. After: every morning starts with a pass, warn or fail, 0 reversed calls.
jobs.not_for: a store that checks numbers once a month and makes no daily calls

jobs.circumstance: the monthly budget review, each platform says it is winning, the store's revenue is less than their total

progress.functional: know each channel's share of real store sales and how much is double counted
progress.emotional: stop feeling played by every platform
progress.social: settle the agency argument with a number both sides accept

jobs.hire_today: a media agency, an analyst, an attribution tool subscription, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the platform screenshots in the agency deck and the habit of adding up platform claims

forces.push: budgets grow on sales that happened once
forces.pull: platform claims set against store orders, with the overlap shown
forces.habit: each platform's number is the one the agency reports
forces.anxiety: what if the true split makes my favourite channel look bad

watch.metric: sum of platform-claimed revenue divided by store revenue, same window, monthly
watch.source: Meta, Google, TikTok reports and Shopify orders

drives.metric: total store sales divided by total ad spend, monthly
